prerequisites: Well-established knowledge of basic Mathematics (especially, resolution of systems of equations, differential and integral calculus)
Well-established knowledge of basic Chemistry (especially those corresponding to Kinetics and Chemical Equilibrium)
Basic knowledge about the First and Second Principles of Thermodynamics, as well as some of the main thermodynamic functions (internal energy, enthalpy, and entropy)

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to formulate and solve material and energy balances in different areas (processes with recirculation, bypass and purge, staged processes, energy production, refrigeration, and gas liquefaction)

Ability to understand the Basic Operations that can integrate a chemical process, the principles on which their design is based, the basic equipment used in them, as well as their applications in the chemical industry.
Ability to understand the types of ideal Chemical Reactors, as well as the fundamentals on which their design is based.
Ability to understand the environmental repercussions of Chemical Processes, as well as the treatment of gaseous, liquid, and solid effluents that may be produced in them.
Know the fundamentals of chemical processes in terms of calculation methods, units, and scientific bases.
Perform material balances of chemical processes with and without chemical reaction.
Perform energy balances of chemical processes with and without chemical reaction.
Know the fundamentals of the main basic operations used in Chemical Engineering.

syllabus_topics: TEMA 09. ENERGY BALANCES IN SEPARATION OPERATIONS
TEMA 11. APPLICATION OF BALANCES IN REACTION EQUIPMENT
assessment_rules: Attendance to Group Tutorials is mandatory, with a minimum of 80% attendance valid in justified cases. Active participation and individual work in each tutorial will be assessed, accounting for 20% of the final grade. The final exam, worth 80% of the final grade, consists of theoretical/practical questions (50% of exam grade) and problem-solving (50% of exam grade). To pass the subject, students must score at least 30% in both the theoretical/practical and problem-solving sections of the exam, and the final exam grade cannot be less than 40% of its maximum value. If all minimums are met and group tutorial attendance is 80% or more, the final grade is calculated as 0.8 * exam grade + 0.2 * average group tutorial grade. Otherwise, the final grade will be the minimum between the calculated grade and 4.0. For students taking early or extraordinary exams before the regular semester, the grade will be calculated using group tutorial grades from the immediately preceding academic year and the extraordinary final exam grade.
